messages:
maria: quick follow-up to the pagination conversation from the RFC — thinking about a flattened iterator shape across py/ts/go that hides pages but gives us a clean place to handle retries. sketch: SDK yields items (not pages). transport exposes per-request retry hooks + a per-iterator policy. pros: easier UX for callers; cons: tricky semantics for prefetch, cancellation, and idempotency. thoughts?

raj: +1 on flattened UX. customers keep asking for simple `for item in result:` semantics.

tyler: main risk is how we surface per-item vs per-page retry failures. if a single page fails mid-prefetch do we retry the whole page or bubble an error for items already yielded?

maria: proposal: yield items as soon as they're available. prefetch should be best-effort. transport will retry page fetches transparently up to N times. if retries exhausted, iterator raises and stops. items already yielded are final.

amanda: what about non-idempotent endpoints? some users expect exactly-once semantics for operations behind pagination (rare but exists).

raj: for non-idempotent flows we should require an explicit flag on the request (e.g., allow_non_idempotent: true) that disables transparent retries and surface page-level errors. default keep retries on.

kevin: Go ergonomics: we typically return (<-chan Item, func cancel, error) or (Iterator{Next() bool, Item() Item, Err() error}). which maps better to flattened semantics?

tyler: Iterator pattern maps well: Next blocks until next item or error. For channels we can send items + close on error, but we lose the error unless we surface a separate Err channel or callback. prefer iterator style for parity.

amanda: Python async: `async for item in client.list_x():` is clean. TS: AsyncGenerator works. both can support `aiter.prefetch(n)` hints? we can add an optional parameter on the client call: `prefetch=2` to hint transport.

maria: yes — add a `prefetch` option on the call config. transport interprets it as concurrency / pipeline depth. default 1.

raj: backoff semantics: do we retry immediately or apply per-iterator exponential backoff? naive per-request backoff may cause head-of-line blocking and higher latency for real-time apps. we should make it configurable: `retry_strategy: immediate|linear|exp_backoff` with sensible defaults per channel (hosted vs private).

tyler: also need to surface attempt metadata for observability (per-page attempt count, last error). console/metrics folks want per-route histograms. add hooks to emit token/route metrics from transport.

maria: agreed. add transport event: `page.fetch.attempt` with attrs.

amanda: cancellation propagation: caller cancels iterator (cancel token or context) -> stop prefetch, cancel in-flight page fetches, and ensure no resource leak. must be consistent across SDKs.

kevin: Go: Context already handles it. Python use `asyncio.CancelledError` semantics. TS use `AbortSignal`. document mapping.

raj: tests: add cross-sdk conformance tests: simulate intermittent page failures, long tail latency, and non-idempotent markers. assert yielded items ordering and error behavior.

maria: migration plan: 1) implement opt-in flattened iterators behind feature flag for each language, 2) run canary user workloads, 3) flip default after 2 weeks of telemetry. Deprecate old page-oriented iterator after 3 months with clear docs.

amanda: one more: edge-case of duplicate items across pages — dedup left to caller? or provide optional dedupe by key?

tyler: offer optional `dedupe_on: "id_field"` param. but document cost and that it requires buffering a seen-set (memory). default: no dedupe.

raj: small nit: ensure SDK errors include a canonical error code for `pagination.retry_exhausted` so apps can do structured handling.

maria: good call. I'll update the RFC follow-up doc and sketch the transport API: `fetch_page(page_token, retry_ctx)` -> returns items + next_token or raises. also a small shim layer that handles prefetch, backoff, and cancellation.

sdk-ci-bot: CI passed for branch rfc/flattened-pagination on main. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

kevin: I'm happy to prototype Go iterator shape this week. assigning self.

maria: thanks everyone. action items: @kevin prototype Go iterator, @amanda add TS AsyncGenerator shim, @raj write conformance tests, @tyler draft observability events. I'll update the RFC with those and call for a decision next Tue. :thumbsup:
